title: Convoy NAKA-303 and Minesweeper No. 15, 5 March 1945
eyebrow: The Tokara Islands · a boat alone against a convoy's escort

participants.name: W-15
participants.note: Minesweeper No. 15, the convoy's leading escort, followed through her own battle report: her position when torpedoed, fixed by bearings on three islands, and her log of those minutes

paras.text: TILEFISH, alone in the Nansei Shoto, found convoy NAKA-303 by its escorts' echo-ranging off the Tokara Islands on the morning of 5 March 1945 and fired three torpedoes at its second freighter. One hit the leading escort, Minesweeper No. 15, which had turned toward the attack: her own battle report and TILEFISH's war patrol report, on one GMT clock.

W-15's report: at 1044 (Tokyo time) one torpedo hit her aft; she broke between frames 96 and 97, her engines and rudder were wrecked and her depth charges caught fire (jacar:C08030608100 p9). TILEFISH's: "Heard explosion four minutes after firing which did not check with torpedo run to AK. Observed CHIDORI escort on fire aft and down by stern. He evidently zigged into our first torpedo" (rg38-74856069/p34). She took the escort for Hatsukari and claimed her damaged. The escorts towed W-15 and beached her off Suwanosejima, where TILEFISH fired two more torpedoes at her at 1707 (K); the escorts' depth charges followed both attacks. JANAC lists Minesweeper No. 15 sunk by a United States submarine on 5 March at 29-30N 129-33E (janac:3/p23), TILEFISH's typed attack position to the minute.

TILEFISH's attack sheet types her noon position for the attack, 29-30.0N 129-33.7E (p33; the narrative's 1200, p15). W-15's position at 1044 is computed from the bearings on her report's sketch (p30): 29-34.8N 129-33.9E, 4.8 nm from TILEFISH's typed position; TILEFISH put her at 3,900 yards. The narrative's "000° 5 miles from Akusekijima" is another 3.3 nm off.

TILEFISH kept zone K (−10); W-15's report is in Tokyo time (I, −9). TILEFISH fired at 1139 K, 1039 I, and heard the explosion at 1143 K, 1043 I; W-15 has the attack on her at 1043 I and the hit at 1044 I.
War patrol report, NARA microfilm M1752 (TILEFISH 74856069). Minesweeper No. 15's Battle Report No. 7 (第十五号掃海艇 戦斗詳報 第七号, 15 March 1945) via JACAR (National Institute for Defense Studies).

Her signal to Sasebo Naval District, sent 0942: at 0833, at this position, heard an explosion; no damage to the convoy (NAKA-303); suppressing (制圧中). At 1000 the escorts broke off the sweep, having found nothing. TILEFISH had not fired: at 0953 K (0853 I) she heard echo ranging at 29-32N 129-31E (contact 11)

Battle Report No. 7's sketch of where she was torpedoed (掃十五被雷位置略圖), convoy NAKA-303: at 1044 Tairajima bore N 15° W, Suwanosejima N 60° E and N 76° E (its two edges), Akusekijima S 1?° E. The narrative (p9) has her 000° 5 miles from Akusekijima
fixes.fix: Computed from the sketch's bearings: Tairajima N 15° W crossed with Suwanosejima's centre (about 068°, between its edges' 060° and 076°), the islands at their Wikipedia coordinates to the minute (Wikipedia coordinates; residual 0.1°). From there Akusekijima bears 167° (S 13° E), as the sketch's partly read S 1?° E; the narrative's 5 miles north of Akusekijima is 3.3 nm from it

events.words: Fired tubes 7, 8 and 9 aft at the second freighter of a convoy of three freighters and three escorts; tube 7 'Missed AK, Hit TB'. The sheet's position is the narrative's 1200 position (p15)

outcome.note: TILEFISH fired tubes 7, 8 and 9 at 1139 K (1039 I) at the second freighter, Hangchow Maru (W-15's No. 2 ship), and heard an explosion at 1143 K (1043 I) that "did not check with torpedo run to AK"; tube 7 "Missed AK Hit TB". W-15's report has her hit aft at 1044 I, having turned toward the wake of the attack on No. 2 ship: one minute from TILEFISH's explosion. TILEFISH took her for "HATSUKARI (CHIDORI Type)(TB)" and claimed her damaged; the ship was Minesweeper No. 15. W-15 counted four torpedoes at her where TILEFISH fired three
The same loss as J01 (her position by cross-bearings), counted once with it

The same loss as J01, counted once with it: her report's summary of the damage, 中破 (moderate), four killed and four wounded, ten days after, beached. TILEFISH claimed her damaged; JANAC credits her sunk

events.title: Minesweeper No. 15
events.words: Results: none. Damage: moderate (中破) … Men: four petty officers and men killed, four wounded … from the middle of the engine room aft she went under water … after grounding, damage to her bottom from the seas

events.translation: Results: none. Damage: moderate (中破) … Men: four petty officers and men killed, four wounded … from the middle of the engine room aft she went under water … after grounding, damage to her bottom from the seas
events.note: The record gives no time; drawn at the time of the attack it matches (Attack 2). Battle Report No. 7's summary (戰果及被害, 15 March 1945), written ten days after the attack with her beached at Kiriishi anchorage, Suwanosejima. Her own reckoning is 中破, moderately damaged; JANAC lists her as sunk (J01's janac). Whether she was later refloated is not in this report

outcome.note: TILEFISH fired two bow tubes at the beached ship at 1707 K (1607 I), saw explosions at 3 min 02 s and 2 min 46 s and claimed two hits. W-15's log: two torpedoes struck the reef about 30 m from her bow, no damage written. The times disagree: 1720 I against 1607-1610 I, 70 minutes, though the two clocks agreed within a minute at Attack 2. The only torpedo attack on her after she was beached in either record, so paired with it; which time is right these pages don't say

pairs.note: TILEFISH fired tubes 7, 8 and 9 at 1139 K (1039 I) at the second freighter, Hangchow Maru (W-15's No. 2 ship), and heard an explosion at 1143 K (1043 I) that "did not check with torpedo run to AK"; tube 7 "Missed AK Hit TB". W-15's report has her hit aft at 1044 I, having turned toward the wake of the attack on No. 2 ship: one minute from TILEFISH's explosion. TILEFISH took her for "HATSUKARI (CHIDORI Type)(TB)" and claimed her damaged; the ship was Minesweeper No. 15. W-15 counted four torpedoes at her where TILEFISH fired three

record.translation: 1043: the enemy submarine attacked us from about 60° to starboard, 1,000 m (four torpedoes). 1044: two torpedoes passed under her bottom, one passed astern, one hit the stern … she broke between frames 96 and 97, the engines stopped and the rudder shaft was wrecked, and she could not steam …
record.note: Her own battle report (written as 本艇, this ship). Before 1043 (104?) she had sighted the wake of the submarine's attack on No. 2 ship Hangchow Maru (杭州丸), 130° to starboard, 1,500 m, and turned hard to starboard toward it. No position written at 1044 but "000° 5 miles from Akusekijima" (p9) and the cross-bearings of p30 (J02)

naka-303.plain: a three-ship Naha–Kagoshima convoy with five escorts, attacked by TILEFISH in the Tokara Islands

voyage.words: 昭和二十年三月三日那覇発鹿児島ニ向フナカ三〇三船団ノ護衛ニ任ズ (to escort convoy NAKA-303, leaving Naha on 3 March 1945 for Kagoshima)
船團ノ位置口之島附近 (the convoy's position, near Kuchinoshima): the Western Sea Escort Force's order to CD-44 and No. 2 Shinto Maru to join and escort NAKA-303, originated 1652, sent 1724

ships.note: Escort No. 1, written 第十五號掃海艇, in her own Battle Report No. 7, 船団編成並ニ護衛艦艇 (the report's writer)
ships.sil_basis: class, assumed: the plate (ONI 41-42, leaf 253) names the No. 13 class, six ships, and Nos. 17 and 18, not No. 15

ships.note: Escort No. 2, written 大安丸; the table's first character is faint (p3), the narrative writes it plainly (p10), when W-15 hands her the command of the convoy after she is hit. By her own signal of 1353 she stayed to guard W-15 at Kiriishi anchorage and sent the convoy on to Kagoshima under Chitose Maru and No. 3 Taihei Maru (p17)
Escort No. 3, written in kana, ちとせ丸
Escort No. 4, written 第五十一播州丸. Left the convoy on 5 March to tow W-15 (Taian Maru's signal of 1353, p17)

Escort No. 5, written 第二號大平丸 in the table (p3). Two signals write No. 3: Taian Maru's of 1353 on 5 March, sending the convoy on with her (第?大平丸, the figure faint, more like 三 than 二, p17), and No. 51 Banshu Maru's of the 6th, meeting 第三號太平丸 near Cape Sata (p19, plain); so do the escort force's order of the 7th (p20) and every line of the escorts' signal log of 5 March (pp22-23, 三號大平丸). Named No. 3 on their evidence; the table's 第二號 stays as written here
Ship No. 1 by the table (type A, maximum speed 8.0 kt), written 杭州丸; the narrative (p9) calls her No. 2 ship (二番船杭州丸), the ship TILEFISH fired at. Her displacement on the table is not read
Ship No. 2 by the table (type A, maximum speed 7.5 kt), written 鳥海丸
Ship No. 3 by the table (type B, maximum speed 7.0 kt), written 鹿島丸

paras.text: NAKA-303 (ナカ三〇三) left Naha on 3 March 1945 for Kagoshima: three ships, Hangchow, Chokai and Kashima Maru, with five escorts led by Minesweeper No. 15 (W-15), whose Battle Report No. 7 is the convoy's record here (jacar:C08030608100 p3). On 5 March, passing north through the Tokara Islands, it was attacked by TILEFISH, who fired at Hangchow Maru and hit W-15 instead (p9; TILEFISH's Patrol 5, Attack 2).
The table numbers the ships 1 to 3 and the narrative calls Hangchow Maru "No. 2 ship"; the order of the column at sea isn't settled by these pages. Its arrival at Kagoshima is not in the pages read.

words.heading: Torpedo Attack No. 2, Patrol No. 5
words.type_attack: Detected pinging on sound gear and commenced closing until twenty minutes later sighted convoy of three freighters and three escorts with single plane escort overhead. Selected second freighter which appeared to be of about 7500 tons, as most likely target. ... Accepted set up of 159° port track, 31 right gyro and torpedo run of 1350 and fired tubes 7, 8, and 9. ... Heard explosion four minutes after firing which did not check with torpedo run to AK. Observed CHIDORI escort on fire aft and down by stern. He evidently zigged into our first torpedo. ... small AK developed into a MARU type escort zero angle on bow, range 1700 yards, narrow beam. Started deep as depth charges began falling.
words.description: Convoy of one medium and two small freighters escorted by one CHIDORI type TB and two MARU type escorts was detected by long scale pinging twenty minutes before sighting masts during conditions of good visibility.
words.determined_by: Observed ship smoking and on fire aft, down by stern, lying to, dead in water.
words.target_line: Target Draft (AK) 10 ft. (TB) 6'9" Course 325 Speed 9 Range (AK) 950 (TB) 3900
words.own_ship: Speed 2.5 kts. Course 134 Depth 63 ft. Angle 0°
words.remarks: Torpedo No. 57819 is believed to have given erratic performance in view of the fact that it was heard running about fifty degrees to the right of its designed course just before its end of run explosion. The misses on the freighter may be accredited to the large track angle presented by a zig at the time of firing ...
words.note: The sheet types two ranges, the AK's (950) and the TB's (3900); attacks.csv keeps the AK's, the target fired at. The hit column types "Missed / AK / Hit TB" on three lines for tube 7. The spread is typed per tube (1½L, 0, 1½R; 1.5L and 1.5R in attacks.csv's offset), the narrative's "spread 1½ divergent" (p14). The ship hit was not Hatsukari: the escort's own battle report puts Minesweeper No. 15 (W-15) torpedoed at 1044 I (1144 K) on 5 March, aft, and she was towed and beached (japanese.yml). The narrative (p14) types the firing at 1139 and the explosions heard at 1143.

words.heading: Torpedo Attack No. 3, Patrol No. 5
words.type_attack: This attack was made on the CHIDORI damaged by attack No. 2, which had been towed and beached by two of the convoy escorts. Both escorts were circling between beached ship and us as we closed to within 2800 yards of beach to fire two bow tubes with zero gyros. No explosions were heard but two columns of black smoke and white spray were observed at target. We started swinging left to open range from beach when escorts were seen to be headed directly for us. At 150 feet, first depth charges began to fall. We are unable to explain the absence of any sound although explosions were observed.
words.description: Same target as attack No. 2. Target had been taken in tow by one of the other escorts while the second escort accompanied them. They were forced to beach the target since it was gradually sinking lower in water. Unable to overtake group while towing but got our shots in after she was beached.
words.determined_by: Observed two columns of smoke and spray at target although heard no explosions.
words.target_line: Target draft 6'9" Course Beached Speed 0 Range 2800 yds
words.remarks: Torpedo run in both cases was close to 2800 yards. Torpedoes were seen to explode three minutes and two seconds, and two minutes and forty-six seconds after firing. Definite explosions were seen at the target although no explosions were heard. Target was resting on beach at time with bow out of water and stern low in water.
words.note: The target's draft is typed 6'9" (6.75 ft in attacks.csv). The narrative (p15): "1605 Sighted our target beached on southeast point of KIRUSHI anchorage with our MARU escort and one trawler type escort circling", and at 1700 "Nip sailors in whites ... lining upper gunwale of target which is beached down by stern, with 15° list".
